decision_reason: This is the historic WordPress theme for data.nasa.gov, not the current data catalog implementation. Its own README says it is out of date and no longer used, directs users to a successor repository, and no source-code license grant is present. Reject: public visibility and NASA inventory metadata do not make this discontinued, unlicensed theme an eligible OSS product.

government_provenance.note: The repository README identifies these files as the old WordPress theme that powered NASA's data.nasa.gov site.

public_source.note: The public repository exposes the WordPress theme files without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The current root file list contains no LICENSE or other source-code grant. The NASA inventory's generic metadata license claim does not substitute for an actual repository grant.

primary_evidence.note: The first-party README explicitly says the theme is out of date and no longer used, and points to nasa/data-nasa-gov-frontpage as the successor; current catalog use of this exact code is not supported.

product_identity: Historic WordPress theme formerly used by NASA's data.nasa.gov portal; not the current data catalog application
license: No exact source-code license grant found in the assigned repository
status_note: Rejected as an obsolete, unlicensed website theme. The assigned repository states it is no longer used and points to a successor; do not transfer this repository's identity or status to that successor.

decision_reason: NASA's exact LAR-17460-1 Software Catalog record identifies DAVEtools, marks it Open Source, and links directly to this repository. The README describes the 0.9.7 Java package and gives detailed command-line, DAVE-ML, MATLAB, and Simulink examples. The repository contains the exact NASA Open Source Agreement v1.3, which is OSI approved, and its initial 2011 source commit already contains the license and functional code. Although GitHub source activity is old, NASA's current product record still distributes this exact tool. Bundled third-party jars remain under their own terms.

government_provenance.note: The exact NASA Software Catalog record identifies DAVEtools as LAR-17460-1 and its Download Now link resolves to the assigned nasa/DAVEtools repository. The repository license names NASA, the same software designation, and LaRC contact Bruce Jackson.

public_source.note: Public repository contains Java source, build files, tests, bundled libraries, the versioned README, examples, and release documentation without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The exact LICENSE.html is NASA Open Source Agreement version 1.3, names NASA and LAR-17460-1/DAVEtools, and grants worldwide rights. NOSA 1.3 is OSI approved (https://opensource.org/license/NASA-1.3). Initial code and LICENSE.html are present in https://github.com/nasa/DAVEtools/commit/b4c30dd1bd124e1b14a14618315069d36721ac21 (2011-08-03). The included third-party jars are separate works and are not newly licensed by this NASA grant.

primary_evidence.note: NASA currently offers this exact open-source software via a direct repository link. The README identifies version 0.9.7 and provides practical commands and worked examples for validation, running models, and generating MATLAB/Simulink outputs; that satisfies versioned reusable-product guidance. The current official NASA distribution supports the quiet-source exception.

product_identity: DAVEtools 0.9.7, NASA's Java package for parsing and exercising DAVE-ML vehicle models and converting them to MATLAB/Simulink, OTIS, and POST artifacts
geography: United States federal aeronautics research; NASA Langley Research Center, Hampton, Virginia
license: NASA Open Source Agreement v1.3 (NASA-1.3) for DAVEtools source; bundled JDOM/Xerces and other third-party libraries retain their separate upstream terms
status_note: NASA's current catalog directly distributes this exact source despite old GitHub activity. The repository bundles third-party JARs whose licenses are not extended by the NOSA grant; describe the entry as DAVEtools, not as a blanket license for those dependencies or external MATLAB/Simulink products.

decision_reason: NASA's ARC-18446-1 catalog page identifies DELTA as an open-source toolkit for deep learning on satellite imagery and links the assigned repository. The NASA Ames README provides Python/GDAL/TensorFlow installation, CLI/library documentation, and training/classification examples. Apache-2.0 applies to the repository source, with functional code and the grant publicly present by 2020; source changes continued into September 2026. DELTA began as one component of the Crisis Mapping Toolkit, but the NASA catalog gives it a separate software designation and the repository is a distinct installable tool.

government_provenance.note: NASA's ARC-18446-1 record identifies DELTA and directly links this repository. The README names NASA Ames Intelligent Robotics Group as developer and describes collaboration with USGS, NGA, NCSA, and the University of Alabama.

public_source.note: Public repository contains the Python package, CLI and model-training/classification code, setup scripts, tests, and documentation. Recent functional changes are visible through 2026-09.

eligible_license.note: The exact repository root LICENSE is Apache License 2.0. The grant was added alongside public functional code in https://github.com/nasa/delta/commit/7d38b52daf66a1afa89d7e7b1cabf641d7ac748b (2020-04-22); third-party software dependencies and imagery retain their own terms.

primary_evidence.note: NASA's current catalog page names the exact DELTA toolkit, describes its satellite-image learning workflow, labels the release Open Source, and links this repository. The README gives working pip/Conda installation and documented training/classification workflows; repository activity includes substantive 2026 code changes.

product_identity: DELTA (Deep Earth Learning, Tools, and Analysis), an installable Python toolkit and library for training and applying deep-learning classifiers to satellite imagery
agency: NASA Ames Research Center, Intelligent Robotics Group
geography: United States federal Earth-science and disaster-response research; NASA Ames Research Center, California
license: Apache-2.0 for repository code; dependencies such as TensorFlow/GDAL/SNAP and training imagery are governed by their own terms
status_note: Distinct product ARC-18446-1 with its own Python package, documentation, and installation path, although NASA describes it as initially used as a component of the Crisis Mapping Toolkit. Keep DELTA and CMT as related but distinct tools; do not treat the CMT integration as license coverage for its independent dependencies.

decision_reason: Coordinator QA found a material license-identity mismatch that the NASA catalog label and README wording do not resolve. The repository's linked LICENSE/DERT_NOSA.pdf identifies its document as “NASA Public License Version 1,” while the README generically calls it NOSA; the currently recognized OSI license is specifically NASA Open Source Agreement v1.3. Until the exact attached terms are compared with NASA-1.3 or another eligible grant is evidenced, the eligible-license check remains unresolved and this project cannot be admitted.

government_provenance.note: The first-party README identifies NASA Ames Intelligent Systems Division as developer, cites NASA mission support and Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter funding, and names collaboration with the MRO Context Camera science team. NASA's ARC-17647-1 catalog record links this same project.

public_source.note: The public repository exposes the Java DERT application source and release files without credentials; the releases page offers desktop binaries.

eligible_license.note: The actual repository license artifact is titled NASA Public License Version 1, not NASA Open Source Agreement v1.3; the repository README calls it NOSA but does not specify a version. OSI lists NASA-1.3 specifically, so equivalence is unproven and requires full-text comparison.

primary_evidence.note: NASA's exact current ARC-17647-1 catalog record describes the DERT viewer and links the assigned source. GitHub publishes versioned DERT v1.0.6 binaries; README explains that Java 1.8 JRE is required and links demonstrations. This versioned release plus runnable-binary/runtime guidance meets the reusable-product notability gate. The current NASA source listing is product-specific distribution evidence despite the quiet repo.

status_note: Held from publication despite clear NASA provenance, public source, versioned release, and documentation. The exact attached license variant has not been shown to be an eligible grant; do not conflate its title with OSI-listed NASA-1.3.

decision_reason: This repository is a set of machine-readable and embeddable representations of NASA's response to the federal digital strategy, not a reusable software product. The README calls its raw-file endpoint a pseudo-service, and the repository has no software license grant or versioned software release. Reject from the software catalog; its government provenance does not convert policy data/schema content into an application.

government_provenance.note: The repository README states NASA's Open Government Team in the Office of the Chief Information Officer coordinated the agency's Digital Strategy implementation.

public_source.note: The public repository exposes HTML, JSON, and XML files without credentials; the README describes raw-file access.

eligible_license.note: The current repository root has no LICENSE file or other source-code grant; public visibility and an inventory license label do not establish permission.

primary_evidence.note: The first-party README describes the repository contents as HTML/JSON/XML action-item representations and a raw-file pseudo-service, not an independently reusable application, operational service implementation, or versioned software product.

product_identity: Static HTML, JSON, and XML representations of NASA's response to the President's Digital Government Strategy; no distinct software product identified
agency: NASA Office of the Chief Information Officer, NASA Open Government Team
